key_insight: CURVE introduces a culturally diverse, multilingual benchmark specifically for long-video reasoning, filling a gap left by western- and English-centric evaluation datasets and enabling more equitable assessment of video models.
problem_solved: Current long-video benchmarks are biased toward Western contexts and English language, limiting evaluation of models' cultural understanding and multilingual reasoning; CURVE provides high-quality, human-generated annotations spanning diverse cultures and languages to address this gap.
method: Curate a long-video dataset with human-generated annotations emphasizing cultural context and multilingual content.
Define reasoning tasks (e.g., long-range QA, temporal and cultural inference) and standardized evaluation protocols/metrics for fair comparison.
Evaluate common long-video models on CURVE to expose cultural and linguistic failure modes and establish baseline performance.
impact: CURVE enables practitioners to audit and improve video models for cultural and linguistic robustness, guiding development of fairer, more globally applicable long-video understanding systems.
visual_elements: World map colored by cultural/region coverage and language diversity (showing non-Western emphasis)
Timeline visualization of a long video with annotated reasoning checkpoints (temporal context illustration)
Bar chart comparing baseline model performance on CURVE vs. existing English-centric benchmarks
Example video frame sequence with multilingual annotation callouts and a sample reasoning QA pair
paper_title: CURVE: A Benchmark for Cultural and Multilingual Long Video Reasoning
paper_authors: Darshan Singh, Arsha Nagrani, Kawshik Manikantan, Harman Singh, Dinesh Tewari
